source_quality.notes: The text layer corrupts every displayed formula, so equations (1) to (52), the four unnumbered protocol rules, Table 2, Table 3, Figure 3 and Figure 10 were read from review proxies. Render pages are 1191 by 1684 pixels at 144 dpi and printed footer page N sits two render pages behind the printed number. The prose is non-native and typo-dense, with slips such as Backgroud, Out Work, costumers and maturer; the slips are preserved rather than corrected.

task_reconstruction.summary: Measure the maturity of a data-and-analytics system on sixteen sub-indicators, rank what to improve first, write protocols for data effectiveness, and test whether customers adopt the metric.

section_map.summary: The summary reports the four requirements in order: the maturity score, the ranking and the advice, the queue and cascade protocols, and the extension with the letter.
Section 1 pairs the growing weight of data with the difficulty of using it, gives each department its own demand, and announces the plan.
Section 2 lists five assumptions with no justification and hands the symbols to one table.
Section 3 defines the sixteen sub-indicators, maps them, weights them by the analytic hierarchy process, and grades the score on five bands.
Section 4 ranks the indicators by PageRank on a causal network and gives hiring, technology and process advice.
Section 5 models transmission as an infinite-server queue, the cascade as a network, and states five protocol rules.
Section 6 scores a randomly generated system at 82.734 and models customer adoption with a replicator equation.
Section 7 lists three strengths and concedes three limits.
Three references, followed by a one-page letter.

contributions.summary: Sixteen sub-indicators split into people, technology and process, ten of them with an explicit ratio.
Three maps, a hyperbolic tangent, an exponential and the identity, chosen by the direction of each indicator.
A PageRank on the causal network offered as the order in which to improve.
A five-rule protocol that grades effectiveness into four named bands.

assumptions.summary: The sub-indicators are comparable with one another.
The transmission rate through every piece of software is the same.
The queue is memoryless: the future state depends only on the current state.
Many companies cooperate with the seaport.
Every customer has the same benefit and the same cost.

data_and_preprocessing.summary: Each indicator is sent through a hyperbolic tangent, an exponential, or left unchanged, depending on whether a rise helps or hurts.
Mapped values are multiplied by 100 so every score lies in [0, 100].
The demonstration uses randomly generated data rather than a real firm.

models.summary: Ten ratio indicators for people, technology and process, with four more left unformulated.
A two-layer analytic hierarchy score with a consistency test and five bands.
A damped PageRank on a sixteen-node causal network.
An M/M/infinity queue whose expected volume is the ratio of the two rates.
A cascade measured by degree and by diameter, graded by five protocol rules.
A replicator equation for the share of customers who adopt the metric.

verification.summary: A judgement matrix is kept only when its consistency ratio stays under 0.1, though no ratio is computed.
The expected queue length recovers the known mean of an infinite-server queue, lambda over mu.
The replicator algebra is correct: the share grows exactly when the benefit exceeds the cost.

results_trace.summary: The people weights sum to one; the technology and process weights each sum to 1.002.
The group scores are 88.240, 67.920 and 86.535, and the maturity is 82.734, inside the Optimizing band.
The lowest scores are multi-workforce, the number of products, and the maintenance rate.
The benefit curves rise fastest when the benefit is high and the cost is low.

writing_logic.summary: Each requirement is compressed into a first-then-finally sequence.
The mapping is motivated by a conflict: a large value sometimes helps and sometimes hurts.
The protocol promises a judgement both in words and in numbers, then delivers four named bands.
The weaknesses bound each method by the job it cannot do.

language_observations.summary: The concept of big data has gained more and more attention these years with the development of information technology.
In the era of data science, it is turning point determining companies to take the lead or be an underdog.
The more experience a staff has, the better work he can achieve theoretically.
We can not afford concrete expression for measuring the data masking level since data are not obtained.
Satisfying at least one of the following conditions, choose hiring.
Apparently, if the utility is below the cost, the cost is not made up.
It is pleasant to tell you that you have made a wise decision.

visualization_observations.summary: Figure 3 draws the sixteen indicators as a causal network, coloured green for people, red for technology and blue for process.
Figure 9 is three radar charts, one per group, and the prose names the lowest point on each.
Figure 10 plots the realized benefit over time for three benefits and three costs.

judge_relevance_hypotheses.summary: A judge can read the result off one number and one band: 82.734 falls in Optimizing, the top band.
Figure 10 is the only evidence offered for the adoption claim, and it is plotted from chosen parameters rather than from data.

weaknesses.summary: The exponential map is increasing, so it rewards the indicators whose rise was supposed to lower maturity.
The normalizing sums in equations (29) to (31) are printed with their limits reversed.
Table 2 gives a matrix of order ten a random index of 0.49, below the value for order nine.
Equation (48) prints the stationary probability with a positive exponential, contradicting equation (47).
Equation (50) calls the cascade level an average but omits the factor one over the number of networks.
The processing-speed rule uses C factorial instead of n factorial and averages raw quantities while claiming the range [0, 1].
The paper concedes the method can only choose among existing options and that time-varying rates would break the protocol.

independent_extensions.summary: Routing each indicator through a map chosen by its direction, before any weighting, would transfer to any maturity score that mixes indicators where a large value sometimes helps and sometimes hurts.

unresolved_questions: Why do equations (29) to (31) sum from i equals 6 or 5 down to 3?
Why does Table 2 give a matrix of order ten a random index of 0.49?
Why does equation (15) use an increasing exponential for indicators whose rise should lower maturity?
Why does equation (48) carry a positive exponential when equation (47) requires a negative one?
Why does equation (50) omit the factor one over N that the prose promises?
Why does the processing-speed tail use C factorial and the positive exponential?
Why does the general effectiveness average the raw quantities yet claim the range from 0 to 1?
Why does the top band drop the percent sign?
Why are the row labels of Table 6 shifted?
What number do the cost breakdown, relevance, consistency and data masking actually contribute?
